node.title: Budget-three fiber-two path constructions share a forbidden factor
node.statement: Let three pairwise-coprime locators be one-root deletions from unions of fibers of a common X^2 map, with completed half-degree s>=2. Writing H_i(Y)=(Y-r_i^2)K_i(Y) gives A_i(X)=(X+r_i)K_i(X^2). The odd and even parts of a nondegenerate three-term relation force all K_i to be scalar multiples of one common K, so the A_i share the nonconstant factor K(X^2), a contradiction. Hence both path-plus-singleton chambers have no direct common-fiber-size-two construction. Together with the Vandermonde theorem, every direct equal-complete-fiber path construction with m>=2 is excluded; m=1, mixed-map, partial-fiber, primitive, and non-path residuals remain open.
